title: False padding in the Boolean code
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, let $L$ be a natural number, and let $a\colon\alpha\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For every natural number $j\ge |\alpha|$, the entry at position $j$ of the Boolean list encoding $a$ with length parameter $L$, using false as the default value beyond the list, is false.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ assigns a Boolean value to each element of $\alpha$
